title: Great Indian Scientists
summary: C. V. Raman, Srinivasa Ramanujan, Jagadish Chandra Bose, A. P. J. Abdul Kalam and Kalpana Chawla.

steps.title: C. V. Raman
sentences: Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman, born in Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu, studied how light scatters in materials.
His discovery, the Raman effect, was announced in 1928.
He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930, and India celebrates National Science Day on 28 February to mark it.

steps.title: Srinivasa Ramanujan
sentences: Srinivasa Ramanujan, born in Erode, was a self-taught mathematician who loved numbers.
He sent his work to the mathematician G. H. Hardy in England and was invited to Cambridge.
He found thousands of results before dying young at 32.

steps.title: J. C. Bose and Kalam
sentences: Jagadish Chandra Bose showed that plants respond to stimuli and built sensitive instruments.
A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, from Rameswaram, helped develop India's rockets and became India's President from 2002 to 2007.
He loved teaching young people and writing books.

steps.title: Kalpana Chawla
sentences: Kalpana Chawla, born in Karnal, Haryana, became the first woman of Indian origin to go to space.
She flew on the Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997 and 2003.
She lost her life in the Columbia accident in 2003 and inspires many young learners.

facts: Ramanujan's number 1729 is called the Hardy-Ramanujan number, the smallest number that is a sum of two cubes in two different ways.
National Science Day in India is celebrated on 28 February.
Kalam was nicknamed the Missile Man of India.
